title: Bind and validate maximal-order worker graph
objective: Bind the precompiled multiprocessing graph to authoritative source/compiler identity, expose a platform memory budget, and register non-skipping regenerated-graph P5 validation

oracles: fresh graph accepted and stale source/compiler identities rejected
registered SEA validation regenerates graph and executes substantive P5 worker tests

runs.command: node --test --test-name-pattern=without a worker host|bounded platform memory|validated precompiled test/multiprocessing-module.cjs

handoff.summary: Bound the allowlisted task graph to exact compiler and canonical Python-source hashes, validate the full source graph before advertising capability and again at module load, expose a host-derived memory budget, and register regenerated-graph P5 plus embedded-SEA validation without burdening ordinary builds.
risks: The substantive arithmetic suite requires the optional FLINT backend, so prepack remains generation-only and test:sea is the authoritative release gate.

The current broad portable tier is blocked by the inherited buchmann_lenstra.py readable-runtime namespace assertion; architecture, strict Python, focused runtime, generated-worker, and SEA checks pass.
next_steps: Run the registered test:sea gate on release CI platforms; the focused python-only SEA smoke already validates the embedded graph identity and exact worker capability.
